text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly commitment-utilization alert fired for eu-north-1. Reserved GPU coverage dropped to 62% between 02:00-04:00 UTC, on-demand spiked.

jonah: link to the dashboard? can we see per-route cost for that window quickly?

maria: https://dash.internal.redwood/finops/commitment-utilization?range=02:00-04:00&europe=eu-north-1

fin-bot: alert: commitment_utilization_low (eu-north-1) - 2026-03-18T02:35Z - impacted_reservation_pool: gpu-a100-40gb-resv-eu - current_coverage=0.62 - threshold=0.75

sarah: Seeing the same in trace — most of the on-demand came from route: chat-stream/redwood-v2-small (long-running inference jobs kicked off by a nightly batch).

kevin: Is that batch scheduled or runaway? If it's scheduled we should pre-warm reserved capacity or move it to a dedicated reserved slot.

anish: quick check on billing lines: the on-demand tags show provider_charge_id=chg-987654, cost_center=ml-prod, egress=low. No suspicious credits applied.

maria: I pulled the per-route cost query for the window:
```
SELECT route, model, SUM(tokens) AS tokens, SUM(cost) AS cost
FROM token_billing
WHERE region='eu-north-1' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-18T02:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-18T04:00:00Z'
GROUP BY route, model
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

ops-bot: runway note: autoscaler scaled up 24 on-demand instances at 02:18 UTC after reserved pool hit 85% util and queued requests > 120s.

jonah: Results look like: chat-stream/redwood-v2-small = $1,420, batch-embed/mini = $340, realtime-chat/mtl = $210. Total on-demand delta = $2.1k for that 2h window.

kevin: Oof. If we had 8 more reserved slots of the same shape that night we would have shaved ~70% of that. Need to run a reservation ROI sim for nightly windows.

anish: Also check whether these jobs could be shifted to lower-cost quantized variants or run in eu-west-2 which has cheaper reserved capacity available overnight. Network egress is minimal so region shift is feasible.

maria: Agreed. Action items: (1) run reservation-sim for eu-north-1 nightly 00:00-06:00 window (2) add a per-route guard in scheduler to prefer reserved pools for known heavy nightly jobs (3) follow up with product to throttle chat-stream batch jobs if non-urgent.

jonah: I'll kick off the sim now and post results in ~30m. tagging @kevin @anish

fin-bot: ticket created: FINOPS-1127 "eu-north nightly reservation sim + scheduler preference" assigned to jonah, priority=high

kevin: For the sim please include: reservation size options (4/8/12), expected monthly incremental commit cost, expected avoided on-demand cost, and break-even months assuming current nightly pattern.

maria: Also include sensitivity: if nightly spikes shift by +/- 1 hour.

jonah: Quick note — historic pattern shows a repeating spike Mon-Fri 02:00-03:30 UTC but weekends are 50% smaller. Will include weekday/weekend split.

anish: If sim looks good, we can do a 30-day trial reserved add-on (short-term reservation) or ask finance for a temporary burst credit. I'll prep the billing rows we need.

maria: One more ask: can ops add a metric in the FinOps dashboard showing "percent of route tokens served from reserved capacity" per hour? That would make these decisions faster.

ops-bot: logged: INFRA-880 "route-level reserved-hit-rate metric" created, pinging eng-infra.

sarah: FYI I checked model config — redwood-v2-small nightly jobs are not pinned to any pool, they use region default. We can add a pool tag to the job spec easily.

kevin: Cool. I'll draft a short runbook for nights: if reserved coverage < 75% and projected on-demand > $500, then either spin short-term reservation or throttle non-critical batch jobs.

maria: Thanks all. Jonah, paste sim output when ready and we'll decide next steps. :thumbsup:
